title: Graph grid and ball bounce data sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Working scientifically, revision through enquiry (Revolution)
source: Written for science/y6 lesson 33 (Graph grid and ball bounce data sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 33: Data: tables, bar charts and line graphs. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

bullets: Units in headings, not in boxes

parts.text: Change goes on the bottom axis: drop height
Measure goes up the side: bounce height
Choose a scale that fits: steps of 10
Plot each point with a small cross, then join

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A straight-ish line going up: higher drop, higher bounce.

keywords.def: rows and columns to record results
a line shows how something changes continuously
the line along the side or bottom of a graph
what the number is measured in, such as cm or °C

questions.q: Temperature of cooling tea every 2 minutes: bar chart or line graph?
Where do units go in a table?
Which axis is the variable you change on?
Core: Draw a line graph of the ball bounce data on the grid. Label the axes with units.
questions.a: Correct axes and units, points plotted, line drawn

questions.q: Extend: Use your graph to predict the bounce from 70 cm.
Stretch: Describe the pattern in one sentence using 'the higher ... the higher ...'.
questions.a: The higher the drop, the higher the bounce.

questions.q: Results for 'which fabric is warmest' need a...
questions.a: B) Bar chart. Fabrics are separate categories, so bars.

questions.q: Big question: which graph shows ice cream sales against temperature best?
questions.a: A line graph (or scatter) because temperature is a number that changes.
